picks.case: Houston’s route is its passing attack: Weigman threw for 343 yards and five touchdowns in the 35–32 Oklahoma State win. That offers a concrete way to pressure Utah. Counterweight: Houston also allowed 32 points; reproducing the scoring output on the road is uncertain.
picks.race_effect: A Houston win would add a head-to-head result against Utah to the Big 12 race; no automatic berth or elimination is asserted.

picks.case: Michigan just held Penn State to 18 points in a 21–18 win. A similarly restrained game creates an upset route against an Indiana offense that scored 15 at Ohio State. Counterweight: those are different opponents; one close result does not establish a predictive defensive advantage.
picks.race_effect: A Michigan win would give Indiana a second consecutive loss and change the Big Ten head-to-head picture; postseason consequences remain conditional.

picks.case: Cincinnati scored 42 against West Virginia, showing a scoring route if this becomes an exchange of possessions at home. Counterweight: it still lost 45–42, while Texas Tech beat Arizona State 53–25. This is a high-risk upset case, not a claim that Cincinnati is the better team.
picks.race_effect: A Cincinnati win would add a conference loss to Texas Tech; the Big 12 title and CFP effects depend on subsequent results.

notes: Three editorial upset cases, not win probabilities or betting recommendations. Each underdog was receiving at least six published points in the October 20 ESPN/Draft Kings snapshot. Lines are reported snapshots and can move. Provider publication times were unavailable; observation times appear on each card in Analysis Mode. USC–Wisconsin was excluded at three points. No public betting splits were verified, so no crowd-based market-trap claim is made.
